A clue about the cat
Tell Ms. Suzuki a new clue about Mike and practise describing places and features in Japanese.
Meet Ms. Suzuki again
Tell Ms. Suzuki the clue
Ah, you're the one who promised to help me the other day! Have you found out anything about Mike?
Ah... sorry. My cat still hasn't been found.
Have you found any clues about the cat?
I saw her near the park.
The cat is the park.
When talking about a place, "~ no chikaku de mimashita" (I saw it near ~) sounds more natural. Please say it again.
Near the shrine. I told you before that Mike likes it there, didn't I?
The park. Oh right, Mike often goes to the park too.
What kind of cat was it?
It was a small white cat.
A white and small cat.
When joining い-adjectives, say "chiisakute". Please say it again.
That's right, that's Mike! Was she wearing a red ribbon on her neck?
Yes, she was wearing a red ribbon.
I don't remember well.
Which side of the park was she on?
On the side across from the convenience store.
Inside the convenience store.
Not inside the store, you mean across from it, right?
Yes, across from it.
You've helped me so much. Thank you for searching with me.
I'll go and look across the way now. Come with me if you can.
Summary: "~ no chikaku de mimashita" (I saw it near ~), joining い-adjectives with 〜くて, "~ no mukaigawa desu" (it's across from ~).
